1. Purpose and scope
This policy sets the minimum customer due diligence (CDD) standards for all clients of the Corporate &
Investment Banking (CIB) division of Meridian Global Bank (MGB). It applies to every booking jurisdiction
unless a jurisdiction addendum sets a stricter or more specific requirement, in which case the addendum
prevails for clients booked in that jurisdiction.
The policy covers new client onboarding, periodic review, event-driven review and exit. It must be read
together with the UBO Identification Standard (MGB-KYC-STD-011), the PEP Standard
(MGB-KYC-STD-012) and the Enhanced Due Diligence Standard (MGB-KYC-STD-013).
2. Roles and responsibilities
•
Relationship Managers (RMs) own the client relationship and collect information and docu

ments from
the client.
•
Onboarding Operations performs the KYC review as maker and the quality check as checker, applying
the four-eyes principle.
•
CIB Compliance advises on high-risk cases and approves cases where this policy or a standard
requires it.
•
Group Financial Crime Compliance (FCC) owns this policy and its interpretation.
3. Client identification
Every client must be identified and verified before any account is opened or any transaction is processed.
Verification uses reliable, independent documents. Identity documents must be unexpired at the time of
verification. The detailed document checklist by entity type is set out in the CIB Client Onboarding
Procedure (MGB-KYC-PROC-010).
4. Risk rating and periodic review
4.1 Client risk rating
Each client receives a risk score from 1 to 100 at onboarding and at every review. The score combines five
factors: client type, jurisdiction, products used, delivery channel and ownership complexity. The score
maps to a risk rating as sh

own in Table 1.

4.2 Periodic review cycles
Clients must be fully reviewed and their KYC refreshed at the frequency set by their risk rating, as shown

addendum cycle applies.
4.3 Overdue reviews
A review not completed within 30 days after its due date is overdue. Overdue High-risk reviews are
reported weekly to the Country Head of CIB, and new transactions for the client require Compliance
approval until the review is completed.
4.4 Trigger events
Certain events require an out-of-cycle review, which must be completed within 30 calendar days of the
event becoming known, regardless of when the next scheduled review is due. Trigger events are:
•
a change of ultimate beneficial owner;
•
an adverse media hit assessed as material;
•
a true sanctions match on the client or a related party;
•
a change in the client's jurisdiction of incorporation;
•
an Unusual Activity Report (UAR) raised on the client.
5. Record keeping
All CDD records, including documents, screening results and approvals, must be retained for at least
seven years after the end of the client relationship.

To: all CIB staff. From: Group Financial Crime Compliance and Global Trade Operations. Date: 17
February 2025.
Changes to KYC periodic review cycles
From 1 March 2025, version 2025.1 of the Global Customer Due Diligence Policy changes the periodic
review cycles. Medium-risk clients move from every 36 months to every 24 months. Low-risk clients move
from every 60 months to every 36 months. High-risk clients remain at every 12 months.
Changes to discrepancy waiver authorities
From 1 April 2025, version 2025.1 of the Trade Discrepancy Waiver Approval Matrix revises the approval
bands and introduces Credit Risk concurrence for waivers over USD 5 million up to USD 20 million.
What you need to do
Read the updated documents on the policy portal. Reviews already sched

uled will be re-dated
automatically.

Global CDD Policy v2026: Consultation Draft

DRAFT FOR CONSULTATION. NOT APPROVED. DO NOT APPLY. Comments to Group FCC by 31 December 2026.
1. Proposed changes
This draft proposes shortening the KYC refresh cycle for High-risk clients from 12 months to 9 months, and introducing continuous monitoring for Medium-risk clients.
2. Rationale
Feedback from the 2026 internal audit indicated that annual reviews of High-risk clients may miss changes in ownership.
3. Consultation questions
Is a 9-month cycle operationally achievable?
What additional resources would be required?

Onboarding FAQ for Relationship Managers


Document ID: MGB-FAQ-060 | Version 2024.2 | Effective 2024-06-10 | Owner: CIB Onboarding Operations | Jurisdiction: GLOBAL




How long does onboarding take?
Most low and medium risk clients are onboarded within two weeks once we have everything we need. High risk clients take about four weeks.


How often will my client be reviewed?
High risk clients are reviewed every year. Medium risk clients are reviewed every three years, and low risk clients every five years.


My client is listed on a stock exchange. Do we still need ownership details?
If the exchange is on our approved list, we only need evidence of the listing.


Can I start a transaction before onboarding is finished?
No. No account can be opened and no transaction processed until onboarding is

approved.


What happens if my client's documents are old?
Proof of address must be recent, and identity documents must not have expired. Ask the client for new copies.

Trade Operations FAQ


Document ID: MGB-FAQ-061 | Version 2025.1 | Effective 2025-05-01 | Owner: Global Trade Operations | Jurisdiction: GLOBAL




How quickly do we check documents under a letter of credit?
Our target is three banking days from presentation.


Can a client ask us to ignore a discrepancy?
The applicant can consent in writing to waive discrepancies. Who approves the waiver depends on the amount. See the waiver approval matrix.


Who do I call about a vessel I'm unsure of?
Escalate to Sanctions before processing the transaction.


What is the cut-off for same-day letter of credit issuance?
Check the trade desk quick reference card for local cut-off times.


How long can a usance letter of credit run?
Up to 360 days without extra approval.

Hong Kong KYC Addendum

1. Application
This addendum applies to all CIB clients booked in Hong Kong and supplements the Global Customer Due Diligence Policy (MGB-KYC-POL-001).
2. Certification of corporate documents
For Hong Kong-incorporated clients, certified true copies of the Business Registration Certificate and the Certificate of Incorporation are required. Certification may be performed by MGB staff who have seen the original, by a certified public accountant, or by a solicitor.
3. Periodic review
Medium-risk clients booked in Hong Kong must be reviewed every 18 months. This overrides the global cycle for Medium-risk clients. High-risk and Low-risk clients follow the global cycles.
4. Trigger events
Trigger events under section 4.4 of the global policy apply in full to Hong Kong clients.

Singapore KYC Addendum

1. Application
This addendum applies to all CIB clients booked in Singapore and supplements the Global Customer Due Diligence Policy (MGB-KYC-POL-001).
2. Beneficial ownership for high-risk clients
For clients rated High risk and booked in Singapore, the threshold for identifying ultimate beneficial owners is lowered from 25% to 10%. Every natural person holding 10% or more of ownership or control must be identified and verified. The global threshold of 25% continues to apply to Low and Medium risk clients.
3. Corporate documents
A current business profile from the Singapore registry, dated within the last 30 days, must be obtained for every Singapore-incorporated client at onboarding and at each periodic review.
4. Periodic review
Singapore clients follow the global periodic review cycles.

1. Purpose
This procedure describes how CIB clients are onboarded, from first contact to account activation. It
implements the Global Customer Due Diligence Policy (MGB-KYC-POL-001) and the CIB Onboarding
Service Level Standard (MGB-OPS-STD-050).
2. Onboarding flow
Every onboarding case moves through eight steps. Steps 5 and 6 must be performed by different people
(four-eyes principle).
1
RM intake: the RM records the client, products and expected activity.
2
Document collection: the RM collects the documents listed in Table 3.
3
Screening: sanctions, PEP and adverse media screening on the client and all related parties.
4
Risk rating: the client risk score is calculated (see MGB-KYC-POL-001 section 4.1).
5
KYC review (maker): Onboarding Operations reviews documents a

nd screening results.
6
Quality check (checker): a second analyst checks the maker's work.
7
Approval: by the approver required for the risk rating and any PEP or EDD conditions.
8
Account activation: accounts are opened and the RM is notified.
3. Rework
If the checker or approver finds missing or incorrect information, the case is returned to the RM. Every
return counts as a rework loop and means the case is not first-time-right.
4. Document checklist
Table 3 lists the minimum documents by entity type. Proof of address must be no more than 3 months old.
Identity documents must be unexpired.

1. Purpose
This standard defines how MGB identifies and verifies the ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) of CIB
clients.
2. Definitions
An ultimate beneficial owner is a natural person who ultimately owns or controls the client.
3. Ownership and control threshold
Any natural person who holds, directly or indirectly, 25% or more of the ownership or voting rights of the
client is a UBO. Any natural person who otherwise exercises control over the client, for example through
the right to appoint the majority of the board, is also a UBO regardless of shareholding. Jurisdiction
addenda may set a lower threshold.
4. Trusts
For trusts and similar legal arrangements, identify and verify the settlor, all trustees, any protector, every
beneficiary with an i

nterest of 25% or more, and any other natural person exercising ultimate effective
control over the trust.
5. Layered ownership
Where there are more than three layers of legal entities between the client and its UBO, the structure is
considered complex and Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) applies under MGB-KYC-STD-013. A structure
chart signed by the client is mandatory.
6. Nominee arrangements
Nominee shareholders and directors must be disclosed. The person on whose behalf the nominee acts
must be identified as if they held the interest directly.

Politically Exposed Persons Standard

1. Purpose
This standard sets out how MGB identifies and manages relationships involving politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members and close associates.
2. Identification
PEP screening is performed at onboarding, at every periodic review and in the daily batch rescreen. A client is PEP-connected if a director, UBO or authorised signatory is a PEP.
3. Approval
Onboarding a domestic PEP-connected client requires approval by the Country Head of Compliance. Onboarding a foreign PEP-connected client requires approval by the Group Head of Financial Crime Compliance (FCC). PEP-connected clients are rated High risk and are subject to EDD.
4. Ongoing monitoring
PEP-connected clients are reviewed every 12 months, in line with the High-risk cycle.
5. Declassification
A person may be declassified as a PEP no earlier than 24 months after leaving the public function, subject to a documented Compliance assessment of residual risk.

1. Purpose
This standard defines when Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) applies and what it requires.
2. EDD triggers
EDD applies when any of the following is true:
•
the client is rated High risk;
•
a director, UBO or signatory is a PEP;
•
there are more than three ownership layers between the client and its UBO;
•
the client has a nexus to a Tier 2 jurisdiction on the Restricted and High-Risk Jurisdictions List
(MGB-SAN-LST-021);
•
the client's business is cash-intensive;
•
material adverse media has been identified.
3. EDD requirements
EDD cases require documentary evidence of the source of wealth (SoW) of each UBO and the source of
funds (SoF) for the expected activity, enhanced ongoing monitoring, and senior approval as set out in
section 5. A site visit is requ

ired for High-risk clients with a Tier 2 jurisdiction nexus.
4. Prohibited structures
Bearer shares are prohibited unless they are immobilised with an MGB-approved custodian. A client with
bearer shares that are not immobilised may not be onboarded.
5. Approval
EDD cases require dual approval by the Country Head of Compliance and the Country Head of CIB.
Meridian Global Bank - Internal
Enhanced Due Diligence Standard
MGB-KYC-STD-013 | v2025.1 | Page 1 of 1

CIB Onboarding Service Level Standard

1. Purpose
This standard defines the service levels for CIB client onboarding and how they are measured.
2. Turnaround time (TAT)
The onboarding TAT target is 10 business days for Low and Medium risk clients and 20 business days for High risk clients. The TAT clock starts when a complete document pack has been received. The clock pauses while the case is waiting for information from the client and restarts when the information is received.
3. First-time-right (FTR)
A case is first-time-right when it is approved without any rework loop back to the RM. The FTR target is 85% of cases each month.
4. Account activation
Accounts must be activated within 1 business day of KYC approval.
5. Reporting
TAT and FTR are reported monthly by country to the Country Head of CIB.

1. Purpose
This policy ensures MGB does not deal with sanctioned persons, entities, vessels or jurisdictions, and
complies with all applicable sanctions regimes.
2. Scope
The policy applies to all CIB clients, transactions and staff in every booking jurisdiction.
3. Screening
Screening is performed at client onboarding, on every trade finance transaction, and in a daily batch
rescreen of the full client base against updated sanctions lists.
4. Potential matches
Every potential match generated by screening must be dispositioned within 24 hours. The analyst must
record the reasons for discounting a match or escalate it as a possible true match.
5. True matches
When a true match is confirmed, all processing must stop immediately. The case must be escalated to
Group Sanctions Advisory w

ithin 2 hours. Staff must not inform the client or any third party of the match or
the escalation (no tipping off).
6. Restricted jurisdictions
Business involving jurisdictions on the Restricted and High-Risk Jurisdictions List (MGB-SAN-LST-021) is
prohibited or subject to EDD, according to the tier of the jurisdiction.

1. Purpose
This procedure sets out how Trade Operations screens trade finance transactions for sanctions risk.
2. What to screen
Every trade transaction must screen all parties and elements: the applicant, the beneficiary, all banks in
the transaction, the vessel by its IMO number, the ports of loading, transhipment and discharge, the
shipping line and carrier, and the goods description against the dual-use goods list.
3. Timing
Screening is performed on receipt of the transaction and again on any amendment that adds or changes a
party, vessel, port or goods description.
4. Vessel red flags
A gap of more than 24 hours in the vessel's AIS (automatic identification system) transmissions during the
past 12 months is a red flag. Other red flags include recent changes of flag or

name and ship-to-ship
transfers in high-risk waters. Any red flag must be escalated to Sanctions before the transaction proceeds.
5. Escalation
Escalations are handled under sections 4 and 5 of the Sanctions Compliance Policy
(MGB-SAN-POL-020).

SBLC and Guarantee Issuance Procedure

1. Purpose
This procedure covers the issuance of standby letters of credit (SBLCs) and bank guarantees for CIB clients.
2. Standard wording
MGB maintains standard templates for SBLCs and guarantees. Use of a standard template with no changes requires only Trade Operations checker approval.
3. Non-standard wording and evergreen clauses
Any non-standard wording requires review by Legal before issuance. An evergreen or auto-extension clause, under which the instrument renews automatically unless cancelled, requires approval by both Legal and Credit, and the instrument must carry a final expiry date no more than 5 years from issuance.
4. Claims
Claims are examined within 3 banking days. Claims under SBLCs are checked against the sanctions screening requirements in MGB-SAN-PROC-022 before payment.

Documentary Collections Procedure


Document ID: MGB-TF-PROC-035 | Version 2025.1 | Effective 2025-02-01 | Owner: Global Trade Operations | Jurisdiction: GLOBAL




1. Purpose


This procedure covers export and import documentary collections handled by MGB.


2. Types of collection


Under documents against payment (D/P), documents are released only when the drawee pays. Under documents against acceptance (D/A), documents are released when the drawee accepts a bill of exchange.


3. Release and follow-up


Documents may be released against acceptance only on the client's written instruction. While a collection remains unpaid, a tracer must be sent to the collecting bank every 30 days.
